title: Formatting datetime col_type issue and extra "\r" included in last column
description:
I have several txt files reading vroom.
Each txt file has seven columns with skipped rows between each line (consecutive new line after contents of last column).

Vroom returns a “\r” at the end of the contents of column 7.  Is there a way to avoid this in vroom?  I know I can gsub the "\r" after, but that defeats the elegance and speed of vroom

Also the fifth column is a date time with format “%b %d, %Y@%H:%M” so I try the col_types argument with X5=col_datetime(format=“%b %d, %Y@%H:%M”) and vroom returns all missing despite having class POSIXct POSIXt.

Any options in vroom to correct these two issues within vroom?
I know I can read as character then convert as.POSIXct(X5, format=("%b %d, %Y@%H:%M")) but that defeats the elegance and speed of vroom.

title: append=TRUE destroys data file if path has compression extension
description:
```r
path <- "test.tsv.gz"
df <- data.frame(A = 1, B = 2)
vroom::vroom_write(df, path)
vroom::vroom_write(df, path, append=TRUE)
vroom::vroom(path)
```

boom, rows are all gone:

```
Rows: 0                                                                                                                                                                    0s
Columns: 2
Delimiter: "\t"
chr [2]: 1, 2
````

If we use an uncompressed path extension (e.g. just make `path = "test.tsv"), then things work as expected.  `readr` and base R are both fine when appending to a compressed file / connection as well.  

We get the same error on `vroom` if we explicitly create the connection with `file(path)` and pass that to `vroom` too.

title: Unable to save tibble with no rows
description:

library(vroom)

# empty tibble
dat <- tibble(
    name = character(),
    date_added = .POSIXct(double()),
)

title: `vroom_write` inherits wrong documentation for `col_names` parameter
description:
Looks like `vroom_write` is inheriting the `col_names` parameter documentation from `readr::read_delim` (via inheriting from `vroom::vroom`), instead of from `readr::write_tsv`. 

These `roxygen2` tags:
https://github.com/r-lib/vroom/blob/488030af21cf9dff6e2aa91df346899397888cdc/R/vroom_write.R#L3-L4

https://github.com/r-lib/vroom/blob/488030af21cf9dff6e2aa91df346899397888cdc/R/vroom.R#L8

Add up to this documentation for `col_names`:
https://github.com/r-lib/vroom/blob/488030af21cf9dff6e2aa91df346899397888cdc/man/vroom_write.Rd#L31-L44

The upshot is incorrect documentation of `col_names` for `vroom_write`, since `readr::read_delim` allows passing a vector of column names in addition to `TRUE` or `FALSE`, while `vroom_write` doesn't.

If you take the above documentation at its word, the following should work (but obviously doesn't):

``` r
library(vroom)
out_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
vroom_write(mtcars, out_file, col_names = paste0("col", 1:11))
#> Error in vroom_write_(xx, path, delim, na_str = na, col_names = col_names, : Expecting a single value: [extent=11].
```

(As a side note, it's also a bit confusing, since the `readr::read_delim` documentation for `col_names` refers to a whole bunch of things that don't really make sense in the context of writing a file)

title: Error in gsub("</", "\\u003c/", payload, fixed = TRUE) :    input string 1 is invalid UTF-8
description:
Hello, I have noticed an error with the specific data that I am working with after reading it using vroom(), and it seems to be caused by some weird value somewhere in my data, but doing the exact same steps using read.csv() does **not** give an error, so I thought I would share my reproducible example here. 

I first got this error when I was testing a package I had not used before and I thought the error was with that package, so I filed and closed an issue there: https://github.com/vegawidget/vlbuildr/issues/54

I noticed the same error again while using vroom and things work fine when I replace vroom() with utils::read.csv():

```
library(pins)
library(DT)
library(vroom)

# Get data from pin
# Register with board - this used to work fine without a token, but you might need to enter yours
board_register_github(name = "github", repo = "ries9112/Pins", branch = "master", token = NULL)

# Pull data from board
cryptoData <- pin_get('cryptoData','github')

# Write to .csv to read it in and convert all data types at once
write.csv(cryptoData, 'cryptoData.csv')

# Read with read.csv adjusts all data types
cryptoData <- utils::read.csv("cryptoData.csv")

# Displaying this table works without issues!
datatable(head(cryptoData, 1000),  style = "default", 
          options = list(scrollX = TRUE))



# Now read with vroom to adjust all data types and do the same thing as before
cryptoData <- vroom::vroom("cryptoData.csv")

# This does not work!
datatable(head(cryptoData, 1000),  style = "default", 
          options = list(scrollX = TRUE))

# This works fine! Somewhere between row 10 and row 1000 there is an issue with a row
datatable(head(cryptoData, 10),  style = "default", 
          options = list(scrollX = TRUE))
```

**If you can't re-create the example, see the GIF I made showing the issue (too large to copy/paste here):** https://drive.google.com/file/d/1UKKtu0me9Ifg_rNXdB-_Mgsv3lkrvAiQ/preview

To summarize what's going on here, first using read.csv() gives no problems at all. Then doing the same steps but using vroom() instead gives the error  ` Error in gsub("</", "\\u003c/", payload, fixed = TRUE) :    input string 1 is invalid UTF-8` But when looking at a preview of only the first 10 rows instead of 1,000 things work with the object created through vroom() as well, which makes me think there is a weirdly formatted value somewhere between rows 10 and row 1,000 that is causing the issue, but I couldn't tell you specifically which value because there are 88 variables and it might take a bit more effort to narrow down the specific issue.

Once again, I'm able to work around this and I don't need a solution, but I wanted to report the issue since this seems odd to me.

title: Does vroom work if there are some blanks in my csv file?
Inconsistent reading of large, irregular CSVs
description:
I have a series of very large (100-million to 10-billion row) CSVs I need to read into R, and I have found serious inconsistencies between how they are handled in readr::read_csv and vroom. No reprex for the moment, but here are the results:

Using the smallest of these files, I have the identical file in .csv and compressed in .gz.

- In both cases, read_csv("file.csv") or read_csv("file.gz") returns a table with 95,196,340 rows.
- For the uncompressed version, vroom("file.csv", delim = ",") returns a table with 89,567,376 rows.
- For the compressed version, vroom("file.gz", delim = ",") returns a table with 46,354,512 rows.

In the terminal, `cat file.csv | wc -l` returns 95,196,347 lines. So read_csv is successfully reading them all, give or take a few which are in fact corrupted, while vroom is failing to read about 7% of rows in the uncompressed file and 52% of rows in the compressed file.

The only obvious (to me) candidate for explaining this discrepancy is that the files are irregular, with most rows missing the final column. read_csv notes this with the usual warning about parsing failures, while vroom is silent. (Both functions succeed in reading the irregular column.)

I would love to be able to use vroom for this data, particularly because the larger files cannot be read in a single go with read_csv because they are too large (https://github.com/tidyverse/readr/issues/1073). But I'm currently prevented from doing so by this issue, and any feedback would be appreciated.

title: `fwf_positions` with start column > end column produces unusual failure behavior.
description:
When calling `vroom_fwf` with a `fwf_positions` call where the start column is above the end column, vroom will error by saying "R character strings are limited to 2^31-1 bytes" rather than a useful user facing error. However, if the user specifies a default column type, vroom will correctly read the file, but produce the character string error when attempting to access the illegally specified column or convert the resulting data frame. 

The example pastebin file described below contains the following text:
```
ABCDE12345hello
FGHIJ67890world
```

```r
library(reprex)
#> Warning: package 'reprex' was built under R version 3.5.2
library(vroom)
#> Warning: package 'vroom' was built under R version 3.5.2
begin_col <- c(1, 6, 11)
end_col <- c(5, 10, 2)
col_names <- c("alpha", "numeral", "error")
positions <- fwf_positions(start = begin_col, 
                           end = end_col, 
                           col_names = col_names)

# Will immediately produce character string error
error_immediately <- vroom_fwf("https://pastebin.com/raw/eRZqfMRd", 
                               col_positions = positions)
#> Error in vroom_fwf_(file, col_positions$begin, col_positions$end, trim_ws = trim_ws, : R character strings are limited to 2^31-1 bytes

error_later <- vroom_fwf("https://pastebin.com/raw/eRZqfMRd", 
                         col_positions = positions,
                         col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
error_later$alpha # Works fine
#> [1] "ABCDE"
error_later$error # Character string error
#> Error in print.default(x): R character strings are limited to 2^31-1 bytes
```

Seems to me that this could be fixed in `fwf_positions` by adding a friendly error if any start > any end (literally `stopifnot(all(start < end))` at a minimum), or else fixed downstream in the compiled library. 

Tagging @deholliday who alerted me to the bug when he ran into it in an upstream package.

title: Filter and Summarize performance on large datasets
description:
Hi - after reading the benchmark blog and vignette, and running my tests on the Taxi dataset and my own large data, I love the performance on the read of files.  vroom uses all available cores... lovely!   But when filtering (or summarizing), it throttles to just a single core.  

I'm wondering if you have any advice as to how to speed this up.  I've tried multi_dplyr, dopar and rmpi, with varying degrees of success.  Here is my "reproducible code" assuming you have the fare data downloaded and unzip'd:

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(vroom)
Sys.setenv("VROOM_SHOW_PROGRESS"="false")
library(tictoc)

filenames <- fs::dir_ls(path="~/trip/",all=TRUE,glob = "*trip_fare*")
tic()
taxiDF <- vroom::vroom(file = filenames, delim=",", escape_double = FALSE) 
toc()
**39.318 sec elapsed**
tic()
taxiDF <- vroom::vroom(file = filenames, delim=",", escape_double = FALSE) %>%
  filter(payment_type != "UNK")
toc()
**206.095 sec elapsed**
```

require(tidyverse)

`x1` is the data as expected while in `x2` all values smaller than 1-60 are `Inf`

vroom is version 1.0.2 and R is 3.6.1

title: dplyr interactions
description:
## Filter / Slice

Ideally these would all return the same as the base subsetting first result, e.g. an un-materialized view on the altrep data.

``` r
library(vroom)
x <- vroom(vroom_example("mtcars.csv", col_types = list()))[1:3]

vroom_str(x[x$cyl == 4, ])
#> 'tbl_df', 'tbl', and 'data.frame': 11 obs., 3 vars.:
#> $model:  altrep:true type:vroom::vroom_chr   length:11   materialized:false
#> $mpg:    altrep:false    type: double    length:11
#> $cyl:    altrep:false    type: double    length:11
vroom_str(dplyr::filter(x, cyl == 4))
#> 'tbl_df', 'tbl', and 'data.frame': 11 obs., 3 vars.:
#> $model:  altrep:false    type: character length:11
#> $mpg:    altrep:false    type: double    length:11
#> $cyl:    altrep:false    type: double    length:11
vroom_str(dplyr::slice(x, which(cyl == 4)))

title: vroom::col_date fails to parse %d%b%Y
description:
Potentially related to #170 and #123. `vroom` seems to fail to parse dates like `29oct2018`:
```r
vroom::vroom("x\n29oct2018\n", col_type = vroom::cols(x = vroom::col_date("%d%b%Y")))
# A tibble: 1 x 1                                                                                                        
  x         
  <date>    
1 NA 
```
Compared with using `readr`, where it's parsed as expected:
```r
readr::read_csv(file =  "x\n29oct2018\n", col_type = readr::cols(x = readr::col_date(format = "%d%b%Y")))
# A tibble: 1 x 1
  x         
  <date>    
1 2018-10-29
```

title: Document how to read and write to C level stdin and stderr
description:
This is something that people working on the command line often want to do, e.g. https://stackoverflow.com/questions/9370609/piping-stdin-to-r

Unfortunately R makes this more difficult than other languages, as the `stdin()` and `stdout()` connections are text mode connections, and also do not really correspond to the C style connections of the same name.

At a minimum we should document this in the getting started vignette or another vignette.

But potentially we could provide a nicer interface that would make this more automatic.

title: Document how reading compressed files work
description:
There has been more than one person wondering about how vroom works with compressed files, if they are uncompressed to a temporary directory etc.

We should add information to http://vroom.r-lib.org/articles/vroom.html#reading-compressed-files explaining how this works.

vroom compresses the file during indexing and writes the uncompressed file to a temporary file in the `VROOM_TEMP_PATH` (defaults to `tempdir()`).

The temporary file remains until it is no longer needed, e.g. the dataset is removed (and garbage collected), all of the data has been materialized or the R session ends. Once this happens the temporary file is automatically cleaned up.

title: vroom::col_date fails to parse single digit month and day
description:
I'm working with about 100 different files mixed between CSV and TSV but otherwise the same (another great reason to `vroom()`).

When I was using `readr::read_csv()` and `readr::read_tsv()` and binding with `dplyr::bind_rows()`, the date column was able to parse just fine with `readr::col_date("%m/%d/%Y")`.

Using the exact same `col_type = cols()` line in `vroom::vroom()` returns many more `NA` values alongside a handful of correctly parsed dates.

Here is the data I get after combining 8 different `readr::read_delim()` tibbles:
```
> dim(nj)
[1] 879485     34
> sample(nj$cont_date, 6)
[1] "2013-02-11" "1993-12-03" "2007-08-13" "1997-10-07" "1997-02-18" "2000-03-10"
> sum(is.na(nj$cont_date))
[1] 4485
```

Here's what I get after doing the same thing in an _awesome_ single `vroom::vroom()` tibble:
```
> dim(nx)
[1] 879485     34
> sample(nx$cont_date, 5)
[1] NA           NA           NA           "2013-10-16" NA 
> sum(is.na(nx$cont_date))
[1] 701768
```

As far as I can tell, all the other columns are parsing fine. Even if I read in the `cont_date` variable as character and parse it after the fact with `readr::parse_date("%m/%d/%Y")`, I get the same data as with `readr::read_delim(col_type = readr::col_date("%m/%d/%Y"))`

Here are the files I'm working with, for reference:

* https://www.elec.state.nj.us/download/Data/Gubernatorial/All_GUB_Text.zip
* https://www.elec.state.nj.us/download/Data/Legislative/All_LEG_Text.zip

title: parsing error when the file contains bad lines
description:
Hi @jimhester 

I noticed some dangerous behavior where `vroom` was silently parsing bad lines in a way that is inconsistent with `read_csv`.

Consider this

```
bogusfile <- '1,2,3
1,2,3
2,1,
1,2,3,4'
```

As you can see, this file contains 3 columns and line 4 is a bogus line with one extra column.

As expected, `read_csv` complains and drops the offending column
```

> read_csv(bogusfile, col_names = c('one', 'two', 'three'))
Warning: 1 parsing failure.
row col  expected    actual         file
  4  -- 3 columns 4 columns literal data

# A tibble: 4 x 3
    one   two three
  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
1     1     2     3
2     1     2     3
3     2     1    NA
4     1     2     3
```

Instead, `vroom` is all happy and actually concatenates the values!
```

> vroom(bogusfile, col_names = c('one', 'two', 'three'), delim = ',')
Observations: 4                                                                                                                                                                                                              
Variables: 3
dbl [2]: one, two

Call `spec()` for a copy-pastable column specification
Specify the column types with `col_types` to quiet this message
# A tibble: 4 x 3
    one   two three
  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
1     1     2     3
2     1     2     3
3     2     1    NA
4     1     2    34
```

This is not ideal. Can we have some arguments where we decide what to do with bad lines? I think you could either mirror what `read_csv` is doing or use Pandas' `error_bad_lines` argument.

What do you think?
Thanks!

title: when specifying col_types, empty strings in a .CSV are read as NA for double, but zero for integer
Documentation Errors
description:
On the vroom site, the documentation under the subheading 'Column type'  on the ['Get Started'](http://vroom.r-lib.org/articles/vroom.html) article appears to be wrong for some of the column types:

- `col_number()` [n], numbers containing the `grouping_mark`
- `col_date(format = "")` [D]: with the locale’s `date_format`.
- `col_time(format = "")` [t]: with the locale’s `time_format`.
- `col_datetime(format = "")` [T]: ISO8601 date times.

This contrasts the documentation for `col_types` for `vroom()` on the [references](http://vroom.r-lib.org/reference/vroom.html) tab:

> Alternatively, you can use a compact string representation where each character represents one column: c = character, i = integer, n = number, d = double, l = logical, f = factor, D = date, T = date time, t = time, ? = guess, or _/- to skip the column.

I was trying to read a date time using `[T]:` and it wasn't until I scanned the reference docs that I found I should be using `T` instead.

I presume this is a mistake in the docs? If not the use of `[T]:` etc. would benefit from more explanation (in my opinion!).

When I read in a series of csv files, null cells are being read in as zero if I specify the col type as integer. Specifying it as double leads to a correct NA. If I don't specify a col type, vroom reads it in as a double and also correctly uses NA.

I checked readr::read_csv and the same file yields NA for both integer and double col types. Similarly, data.table::fread produces an integer type and NA value.

title: vroom setDT performance
description:
Hi,

I'm wanting to use vroom and then change to a `data.table` so that can use the data.table syntax for manipulation. Whilst the import speed is amazing compared to **feather** (what I'm currently using), when converting to data.table something weird is happening, where it is taking significantly more time for **vroom** than **feather**. Is there something going on in the back of vroom to cause this?

```
library(data.table)
library(feather)
library(vroom)
library(microbenchmark)

ft <- data.frame(X = seq(1e7), Y = rep(letters[1:25]), Z = rep(c(TRUE, FALSE), each = 10), 
                 W = paste(LETTERS[1:25], collapse = ""), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
fwrite(ft, "test.csv")
write_feather(ft, "test.feather")

func_a <- function() {
  dt <- vroom("test.csv", col_types = "iclc")
}

func_b <- function() {
  dt2 <- read_feather("test.feather")
}

func_c <- function() {
  dt <- vroom("test.csv", col_types = "iclc")
  attr(dt, "spec") <- NULL
  setDT(dt)
  dt
}

func_d <- function() {
  dt2 <- read_feather("test.feather")
  setDT(dt2)
  dt2
}

microbenchmark(
  VROOM = func_a(),
  FEATHER = func_b(),
  VROOM_DT = func_c(),
  FEATHER_DT = func_d(),
  times = 10
)
```

title: Issue with reading large compressed file (.zip and .gz)
description:
My use case is trying to avoid to load some data into Apache Spark and instead use the fantastic vroom package (thanks!) to read a large compressed file with occurrence data, in order to then be able to check if there are any duplicates in one column called "occurrenceID".

The dataset I am using is available for download here: http://www.gbif.se/ipt/archive.do?r=artdata 

It contains an occurrence.txt file which is approx 70 GB when unpacked. 

I my attempt to read the data I use compressed files - one is the original file from the earlier download link meaning it is a .zip-file (DarwinCore Archive file) with that occurrence.txt file inside and the other one is a .gz of that occurrence.txt file. 

The .zip file is 5.7 GB and the .gz file is 5.2 GB on disk.

To test this approach I start R with tidyverse and install the vroom package:

```bash
# /data is mounted and holds the .zip and .gz files
docker run --rm -it -v archive-docker_data_archive:/data:ro rocker/tidyverse:3.6.0 bash
```
I then issue these commands after starting R:

```r
install.packages("vroom")

library(vroom)

# attempt 1
df <- vroom("/data/artportalen/artdata.zip", col_select = "occurrenceID")
```
This gives this message:

```
Multiple files in zip: reading 'occurrence.txt'
Error in vroom_(file, delim = delim, col_names = col_names, col_types = col_types,  : 
  Evaluation error: Unknown column `occurrenceID` 
Call `rlang::last_error()` to see a backtrace.
In addition: Warning message:
In (function (con, what, n = 1L, size = NA_integer_, signed = TRUE,  :
  possible truncation of >= 4GB file
```

So to work around the .zip limit I instead attempt to use a .gz variant of the same occurrence.txt data.

```r
# attempt #2
df <- vroom("/data/artportalen/artdata-occ.gz", col_select = "occurrenceID")

# .... progress is reported indexing over 100 GB for around 10m, then ...
```

This causes a segfault:

```
 *** caught segfault ***
address 0x7fbd515ae292, cause 'memory not mapped'

Traceback:
 1: vroom_(file, delim = delim, col_names = col_names, col_types = col_types,     id = id, skip = skip, col_select = col_select, na = na, quote = quote,     trim_ws = trim_ws, escape_double = escape_double, escape_backslash = escape_backslash,     comment = comment, locale = locale, guess_max = guess_max,     n_max = n_max, altrep_opts = vroom_altrep_opts(altrep_opts),     num_threads = num_threads, progress = progress)
 2: vroom("/data/artportalen/artdata-occ.gz", col_select = "occurrenceID")

Possible actions:
1: abort (with core dump, if enabled)
2: normal R exit
3: exit R without saving workspace
4: exit R saving workspace
Selection: 

```

Both attempts fail.

The attempt with the .zip file complains about the column name being faulty, but I think it is not misspelled and perhaps a consequence of an interrupted read, the error message leads me to this SO post which I don't know how to work around:

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42740206/r-possible-truncation-of-4gb-file

The attempt with the .gz file appears to read more than a 100 GB before it crashes, which is strange since the file is 5.2 GB compressed which should be less than 70 GB when unpacked. 

Therefore reporting this as a possible bug.

description:

# libraries ---------------------------------------------------------------

library(tidyverse)
library(vroom)

# raw data ----------------------------------------------------------------

my_file <- "https://nces.ed.gov/ipeds/datacenter/data/EF2017A_Data_Stata.zip"

temp <- tempfile()

download.file(url = my_file, temp)

dat <- vroom(unz(temp, "ef2017a_data_stata.csv"))
```

title: Consider an occupancy bitmap
description:
Columns could store a vector of the values and as they are accessed with the altrep element accessors mark off which values have been read and store the values in the vector. Then on further element wise operations it would just check the occupancy bitmap to see if the value had already been read, and if so then to return the stored value. When all the values have been read the vector can then be used directly as the materialized vector.

This would fix the problem of multiple different element-wise accesses reading the same data from disk multiple times, at the cost of some more memory up front.

title: Understanding vroom performance
description:
Hi,

I've finally found some time to try replacing readr with vroom in my R package: whilst it is clearly working as intended understanding how it works differently to readr is obviously critical. I'm kind of asking questions here, but it may be a helpful issue to generate a vignette from in future.

I have a function, read_ssnap_csv that uses readr to load the CSV and then perform the tidying. I've duplicated it as read_audit_csv, and swapped out readr for vroom.

What I've discovered so far is that if I use vroom I get significant speed gains loading my R file. I took the functions and stopped the code after the file read operation:

This is vroom:
```
                                                      expr      min       lq     mean
 ssnapinterface::read_audit_csv("../SSNAPTestData316.csv") 61.48958 70.04886 110.3929
   median       uq      max neval
 96.73592 110.6406 294.9985    10

```

This is readr:
```
Unit: milliseconds
                                                               expr      min       lq
 ssnapinterface::read_ssnap_csv("../SSNAPTestData316.csv", "3.1.6") 125.0023 127.4047
     mean   median       uq      max neval
 169.9288 137.0685 216.3664 273.7023    10

```

However, the functions then undertake some tidying of the data using a set of dplyr functions (mutate, filter, etc).

After tidying, we lose all that advantage and vroom ends up much slower than readr:

Vroom:
```
                                                      expr     min       lq     mean
 ssnapinterface::read_audit_csv("../SSNAPTestData316.csv") 535.522 546.9812 585.3708
   median       uq      max neval
 554.6229 569.3828 829.7836    10

```

Readr:
```
Unit: milliseconds
                                                               expr      min       lq
 ssnapinterface::read_ssnap_csv("../SSNAPTestData316.csv", "3.1.6") 308.5204 327.5631
     mean   median       uq      max neval
 375.7263 353.3448 412.5121 520.2157    10

```

So clearly the type and usage of functions to process vroom data is really important. Are there ways to tidy the data which are more 'vroom-friendly'? Any obvious dos and don'ts based upon how vroom works which might explain this big difference?

title: Commas inside quoted fields breaks column reading
description:
I've had trouble importing a text file this morning; when I've looked at it I think this is an issue with delimiter reading in combination with quoted fields.

For reasons not known to me, I'm given CSV files where all field values are quoted "". In one field there are two comma delimiters within the quoted text, which is being interpreted as being three column values. Subsequently this then throws the rest of the files out.

Possibly complicating this is the use of col_guess() for undefined columns (including the column in question) as these columns are custom fields.

I've tried to build a reproducible example - Dogs.txt doesn't quite exhibit the problem I wanted, but exhibits enough problems that it probably encapsulates the issue.

If we load dogs.txt with:

```
dog_cols <- readr::cols(Animal = readr::col_character(), Legs = readr::col_integer(), Comments = readr::col_character(), Owners = readr::col_integer(), HasTeeth = readr::col_logical())
test <- vroom::vroom("../Team Data/Dogs.txt", col_types = dog_cols)

```

> Error in vroom_(file, delim = delim, col_names = col_names, col_types = col_types,  :                                           
>   Not compatible with STRSXP: [type=NULL].
> 

If we specify the delimiter:

`test <- vroom::vroom("../Team Data/Dogs.txt", col_types = dog_cols, delim = ",")
`
We also fail.

If we test the same code in readr:

`test <- readr::read_csv("../Team Data/Dogs.txt", col_types = dog_cols)
`

> Warning: 1 parsing failure.
> row col  expected    actual                    file
>   2  -- 6 columns 5 columns '../Team Data/Dogs.txt'
> 
> Warning message:
> Missing column names filled in: 'X6' [6] 
> 

Then the code will read but will insert an extra column at the end (so this may be a readr issue rather than a vroom one, albeit the error codes are different.

[Dogs.txt](https://github.com/jimhester/vroom/files/2999330/Dogs.txt)

title: Performance parsing doubles
description:
We should be able to go faster than we are

```r
create_df <- function(rows, cols) {
  as.data.frame(setNames(
    replicate(cols, runif(rows, 1, 100), simplify = FALSE),
    rep_len(c("x", letters), cols)))
}

df <- create_df(1000000, 10)
readr::write_csv(df, "long.csv")
bench::system_time(data.table::fread("long.csv"))
#> process    real
#>  931ms   161ms
bench::system_time(vroom::vroom("long.csv"))
#> process    real
#>  820ms   134ms

title: Add `Get_region` implementations for numeric types
description: These are used internally by R for sum, mean, min, product and some other things. Should make them a bit faster than they are currently, as the default method calls `Get()` for each element in turn, which has additional function call overhead, in addition to extra calculations to determine the offset.

title: Re-use memory when materializing vector
description: Currently `get_trimmed_val()` returns a new string object, so memory needs to be dynamically allocated for each one. We could instead reuse the same block of memory for each value.

title: All connection are in use when opening many compressed csvs
description:
Not sure if this is the reason for #20, but when opening many compressed CSV files (e.g., `.csv.xz`), I get the following warning: `Error in xzfile(path, "") : all connections are in use`.

Toy example:
```
t_dir <- tempdir()
for (i in 1:1000) {
    readr::write_csv(
        tibble::tibble(
            x = rnorm(1000), 
            y = rnorm(1000)
        ), 
        sprintf("%s/%s.csv.xz", t_dir, i)
    )
}
vroom::vroom(fs::dir_ls(t_dir, glob = "*.csv.xz"))
```
